transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor... my wife, she's the one who wanted me to come in. She says it's all just talk, but... well, I came because of the men at the domino table. We play over at the center. You know, that building used to be a hardware store back in the fifties. I bought my first good hammer there before I had to leave school to go work. I still have it, too. Good heavy wood handle, not like the cheap plastic nonsense they sell nowadays. 

But anyway... those men at the table, and sometimes the announcer on the radio... they give these little messages. Just meant for me. I leave the radio on in the kitchen most mornings because it keeps the house from feeling so quiet, especially since we don't get as many birds in the yard as we used to. But I hear what that announcer is saying. Even with my wife telling me to hush and that it's just regular talk, I know better. I know they are warning me to be careful. You just... you can't be too careful.
Do you think these messages from the men at the domino table and the radio announcer are meant for you alone, or could they also be meant for someone else?

Oh, they're just for me. Nobody else. My wife, she keeps saying, "It's just regular talk, you're making something out of nothing." But I know better. I know they are warning me to be careful. And you really do have to be careful... especially with how things are now. 

Like the weather, for instance. It rained so hard last Tuesday it completely washed out my tomato plants. I've been growing those Big Boy tomatoes in that exact same patch of dirt by the chain-link fence since... oh, must be 1978. My neighbor, he tried to tell me I ought to use those raised beds. Raised beds! I told him my knees aren't what they used to be, but I'm sure not building a wooden box just to grow a decent tomato. Have you seen the price of lumber lately? I went down to the yard to get a couple of two-by-fours last month to fix the porch step and nearly fell over. It’s highway robbery, that's what it is. Back when I was working, you could get... 

But... well, what was I saying? Oh. Yes, the messages. I don't know about anyone else, but those little messages from the announcer and the men playing dominoes... they're definitely just meant for me.
Do you feel like your thoughts are connected and make sense when you're talking, or do you sometimes find it hard to stay on one topic?

Well, sometimes it feels like... like my mind is just running a mile a minute. It goes from thinking about the church choir on Sunday, to that baseball game I watched, then over to the repairs on the porch, and then to my friend down the street... all just bouncing around so fast. I can't even hold onto one thought long enough to explain it right to my wife. 

Speaking of the choir, though, they got a new director a few months back. Young fellow, probably no older than thirty. He’s got them singing all these new arrangements. It’s not like the old hymns we used to sing. I remember when I was a boy, my mother used to sing "Rock of Ages" while she was washing the dishes. She had this old porcelain sink, the kind with the double basin, and it would get these dark scratches on the bottom if you scrubbed it too hard with the steel wool. You don't see sinks like that anymore. Now it's all stainless steel. They say it's easier to clean, but I think it looks too cold. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right. My thoughts. Yes, they just go so fast from one thing to another, it's hard to keep them straight.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other when you're talking?

Well, disconnected... I don't know if I'd say disconnected. It's more like they just... they just get away from me, you know? Like I was saying, they go so fast. It's like trying to catch a firefly in a jar when you're a kid. We used to do that all summer long out by the old oak tree in the front yard. That tree had to be a hundred years old. Lightning struck it back in '92, split a whole branch right down the middle. Sounded like a cannon going off in the living room. My wife thought the roof caved in. We had to call the tree service, and this fella came out with a bucket truck... 

But, disconnected? I'm not sure what you mean by that, exactly. They're all my thoughts, they just... they just don't like to stay put.
Do you believe that the messages from the radio announcer and the men at the domino table are trying to tell you something specific about your life or actions?

Well, yes, like I was saying before... they are definitely warning me to be careful. That's the specific thing. My wife, she just rolls her eyes and says it's regular talk, but I know a warning when I hear one. You really do have to keep your eyes open these days. There's a lot to be careful about out there. 

Just take the traffic on my street, for example. People drive like absolute maniacs now. Used to be you could let a dog wander out front without a worry in the world. We had a little terrier mix, Buster, back when the kids were small. Smartest dog you ever saw. He could balance a milk-bone on his nose until you said the word. We got him from my brother-in-law, Frank. Frank worked down at the auto plant for thirty years before they closed it up. It was a real shame when that happened, a lot of good men out of work. Frank ended up moving down to Florida, bought a little place near the water... says the humidity is good for his joints, but I don't know how anyone stands that heat all year round. I went down there once in August and thought I was going to melt right to the pavement. 

But, uh... what was I... oh, yes. The radio announcer and the men playing dominoes. They slip those little messages in just for me, telling me to be careful. That's exactly what they're trying to tell me.
Do you ever feel like the messages you're hearing are not real?

Not real? No, no, they're as real as you sitting right there. I mean, I told you why I came in today, right? It's because of those messages. The men down at the domino table, and the fella on the radio... they give these little messages meant just for me. My wife, bless her heart, she says it's just regular talk, that I'm making it up. But I know what I hear. I know they're warning me to be careful. 

You know, my wife has always been a bit hard of hearing, though she won't admit it. She keeps the television turned up so loud the neighbors could probably hear Pat Sajak calling out the letters. We bought that TV back in... oh, it must have been '08. One of those big flat screens. Our grandson came over and mounted it right on the wall for us. He's a good boy, works in computers over in the city. Makes a good living, but he works too many hours if you ask me. I always tell him, you've got to make time to enjoy life, maybe go fishing once in a while. I used to love fishing down at the creek when I was his age. Caught a catfish once that was as long as my arm. Fought me for twenty minutes before I finally got him on the bank. 

But anyway, no, those messages are real. They're definitely real, and they're telling me to watch my step.
Do you ever feel like you're losing touch with what's real and what's not?

Losing touch with what's real? Well, I don't know about losing touch, but... well, some afternoons, when the house gets real quiet, I hear things. Like my old friend, Charlie. I'll hear him call my name right from the front porch, or sometimes he's just humming one of those old choir songs we used to sing. Clear as day, like he's standing right there next to me. 

Charlie and I, we sang in the church choir for near on forty years. He had this deep baritone voice, could rattle the stained glass windows on a Sunday morning if he really let it out. We used to practice on Tuesday nights, and afterward, we'd always stop at the diner on Main Street for a slice of cherry pie. They had the best cherry pie in town. The crust was always perfectly flaky, made with real lard, not that shortening stuff they use now. You just can't find a good pie crust anymore. The lady who ran the place, Martha, she retired back in... oh, must have been '98, and her son took over. He changed the whole menu, put in all these fancy coffees. Ruined the place, if you ask me. 

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right, Charlie. Yeah, I hear him sometimes, clear as a bell, just humming away on the porch. So I guess... I don't know if that's losing touch, but it sure feels real to me.
Do you think the messages from the radio announcer and the men at the domino table could be related to your own thoughts or are they completely separate?

My own thoughts? No, no, they are completely separate. I mean, doctor, like I said, that's exactly why I came in here to see you. The men at the domino table, and sometimes the radio announcer... they give these little messages meant just for me. It's not just me thinking it up. Even when my wife says it is just talk, I know they are warning me to be careful. 

She's always telling me I spend too much time in my own head, just sitting in my old armchair stewing on things. I've had that chair since... gosh, since before the old mill closed down. Bought it at a yard sale over on Elm Street for five dollars. You just can't find a good sturdy chair like that anymore. Everything nowadays is made of that cheap particle board. My neighbor, Bill, he bought a whole new dining set from one of those big warehouse stores, and I kid you not, the leg snapped right off on Thanksgiving Day. Sent the turkey and the gravy flying all over his wife's good rug. It was one of those fancy Persian rugs, too. Bill was so red in the face I thought he was gonna have a heart attack right there in the dining room. He spent three days trying to get that gravy stain out with club soda and vinegar. 

But... well, anyway, what were we saying? Oh, the thoughts. No, the messages aren't my own thoughts. They're coming right from them, telling me to watch out.
Do you think it's possible that the messages you're hearing are just your own mind interpreting things, rather than actual messages from the radio announcer or the men at the domino table?

My own mind? Now, doctor, I feel like we just went round and round about this. My mind isn't playing tricks on me or... or interpreting things wrong. I might be getting up there in years, but my head works just fine. 

Speaking of minds playing tricks, though, you know my older brother, Frank... well, God rest his soul, towards the end, his mind really did go on him. He started thinking the mailman was stealing his National Geographic magazines. Used to wait by the mailbox with a broom to chase the poor fella off. It was a crying shame, really. Frank had a subscription to that magazine since... oh, 1962, I reckon. Kept every single issue stacked up in his garage. The fire marshal came by once and said it was a hazard, but Frank wouldn't let anyone touch them. He always loved reading about the jungle, said he was gonna go down to the Amazon river one day and see those colorful birds. Never made it further than the county line, though. Worked at the tire plant his whole life until his back gave out on him. They gave him a gold watch when he retired, but it stopped ticking after a month. Cheap thing. 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, about my mind making it up. No, I'm not like Frank was. Like I keep trying to tell you, I came in here because those men down at the domino table, and that announcer on the radio... they really are giving me little messages meant just for me. Even when my wife rolls her eyes and says it's just regular talk, I know better. I know they are warning me to be careful, and a man's gotta listen when he's being warned.
Do you often find it difficult to keep your thoughts in order when speaking?

Keep my thoughts in order? Well, I reckon it is hard sometimes. It gets awful crowded up in my head. My mind just runs from the choir to baseball to repairs to my friend and back again... just goes so fast that I cannot hold one thought long enough to explain it right to anybody. 

Speaking of baseball, I was just thinking the other day about the old minor league team we used to have down by the river. We'd go down there on a Friday night, get a hot dog for fifty cents. Fifty cents! You can't even buy a stick of gum for that now. I tried to buy some of that peppermint gum at the pharmacy last Tuesday when I was getting my wife's foot cream, and the girl behind the counter wanted two whole dollars. Two dollars for gum! And she was chewing a piece right there while she rang me up, just smacking her lips. No manners at all. My mother would've washed her mouth out with soap for that. Palmolive, usually. Tasted awful, let me tell you, but it sure did the trick. We used to keep a bar of it right by the kitchen sink, in this little ceramic dish shaped like a turtle... 

But, uh... what were you asking me? Oh, right, my thoughts. Yeah, they just jump around like that, faster than I can catch 'em.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumping between ideas without any connection between them?

Without connection? No, no, I wouldn't say that. To me, they always connect up just fine. It's like tying knots, you see. You tie one piece of string to another, and it all makes a line. My grandfather taught me how to tie a proper bowline knot when we used to go fishing out on Lake Moccasin. We had this little aluminum boat... leaked like a sieve, I tell you. Had to bring an old coffee can just to bail the water out so we wouldn't sink. It was a Folgers can, back when they made them out of real tin, not that cheap plastic they use today. My wife, she takes those plastic tubs now and uses them to hold her sewing buttons. She's got hundreds of buttons in there. I don't know why anyone needs so many. I lost one off my good Sunday shirt last week, and she sewed on this shiny pearl one by mistake. Looked awful foolish on a plain blue shirt. I told her to take it off, but she said I was being fussy. Fussy! Can you believe that? After all the years I... wait, what was it you just asked me? Something about a connection?
Do you think the messages could be something you're telling yourself, rather than actually hearing them from the radio or the men at the domino table?

Now, Doc, didn't we just go over this? I feel like a broken record sitting here. I ain't telling myself anything. Like I said before, I came in here because the men at the domino table, and sometimes that fella on the radio... they really are giving little messages meant just for me. 

My wife, she always tells me it's just regular talk. But she does a whole lot of talking herself, you know. Mostly on the telephone with her sister Margaret out in Omaha. Margaret sends us a big box of those frozen steaks every Christmas. Good meat, I suppose, but they pack it in that dry ice. You gotta be real careful with dry ice. I burned my thumb on a piece of it back in '78 when we had that bad blizzard and the power went out for three days. We had to keep the milk cold out on the back porch... but the raccoons got to it anyway. Darn critters are smart, I tell you. They can open a latch just like a person with hands. Caught one in the garage once trying to get into my bait cooler, and he just looked right at me, bold as brass. Plump thing, too, probably been eating all the neighbor's cat food...

Wait, what were we just talking about? Oh, the messages. Right. No, I'm not making it up in my head. Even if my wife thinks it's just talk, I know what I hear. I know they are warning me to be careful. And a man's gotta be careful these days.
Do you think there's a possibility that the messages you're hearing are not actually being sent by the men at the domino table or the radio announcer, but are rather a product of your own thoughts?

Well, I... I thought we just settled that. It's like you're not hearing me, Doc. I'm telling you, it ain't my own thoughts. I came in here because of those men down at the domino table, and that fellow on the radio. They're giving me little messages, meant just for me. 

Now, my wife, she says the exact same thing you're saying. "It's just talk, Arthur," she says. She says that while she's watching her game shows. She loves that Wheel of Fortune. Never misses an evening. I don't care for it much myself, all that clapping and hollering over a puzzle. I prefer the old westerns. Gunsmoke, Bonanza. Now there was a show. You don't see horses like that on TV anymore. Beautiful animals. My uncle used to keep a couple of roans out on his farm when I was a boy. I'd help him muck out the stalls on Saturday mornings. Hard work, let me tell you, but it built character. We'd use this big old pitchfork, handle was worn smooth as glass from years of holding it. I got a splinter the size of a matchstick in my palm once, had to soak it in hot water and Epsom salts for two days before my aunt could dig it out with a sewing needle... 

But, uh, what was I... right, the radio and the dominoes. No, it's not my own thoughts. I know what I hear. Even if my wife thinks it's just talk, I know they are warning me to be careful. You can't be too careful, you know.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds when there's no one around and no radio or TV is playing?

Well, now that you mention it... some afternoons, when the house gets real quiet, I do hear my old friend. He calls my name right from the front porch, or sometimes he's humming an old choir song. It's so clear, it's just like he is standing right there. 

We used to sit on that porch for hours, him and me. I built that porch myself, you know, back in '62. Used good solid pine. You can't get wood like that anymore, all the lumber yards sell that cheap stuff that warps after one good rain. I painted it a nice slate gray, though my wife, she wanted white. I told her, 'Mary, white is just gonna show every speck of dust when the wind blows off the road.' Course, the road wasn't paved back then. It was all dirt and gravel until the county finally came through and blacktopped it. Must have been the same year they put in that stoplight down by the hardware store. That light takes forever to change. I sat there for five minutes Tuesday, just me and a fellow in a red Ford... 

What was I... oh, right. The quiet. Yeah, when the TV is off and it's real still, I hear him calling from the porch. Clear as day.
Do you think your mind is playing tricks on you when you hear these messages?

Doc, I swear we keep going in circles here. My mind ain't playing tricks. I'm telling you, I came in here because the men at the domino table, and sometimes that fella on the radio... they are giving me little messages. It's meant just for me. 

My wife Mary, she says the same thing you do. 'It's just talk, Arthur,' she says. She always thinks she knows best, especially when it comes to the garden. She's got this idea that you can't plant tomatoes until after the first full moon in May. I tell her, the ground's warm enough by mid-April if we don't get a late frost. We had a frost back in '93 that killed off every single seedling I put in the ground. Had to drive all the way over to the nursery in the next county to buy new ones. They had this big orange cat living in the greenhouse there, fattest thing you ever saw. Just slept on the bags of potting soil all day. I had a cat like that when I was a boy, named him Barnaby. He was a good mouser, kept the barn clear of rats...

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, the messages. Right. No, my mind is fine. Even when Mary says it's just talk, I know what I'm hearing. I know they are warning me to be careful. And I'm going to listen.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumping around in a way that doesn't make sense to you?

Well... yeah, I suppose they do jump around a fair bit. It's like... my mind runs from the choir, then over to baseball, then I'm thinking about those repairs on the porch, and then back to my old friend... it goes so fast I just can't hold onto one thought long enough to explain it right to you. 

It's like watching a baseball game on the television when they keep switching the camera angles. I used to love listening to the games on the radio, though. The announcer would paint a picture so clear you could smell the hot dogs. We used to go to the minor league games down at the old stadium before they tore it down in '88. They built that new shopping center over it. Got a big hardware store in there now, but they don't carry the right kind of nails for roofing. I needed galvanized roofing nails last summer when the wind ripped a few shingles off the shed. I patched it up myself, though my knees ain't what they used to be. Getting up on that ladder was a chore. I had to borrow my neighbor's ladder because mine got a crack in the side rail...

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, my thoughts. Yeah, they just race from one thing to the next, real fast like. Can't hardly catch 'em sometimes.
Do you think the way your thoughts jump around is affecting your daily life?

Well, I suppose it is. I mean, I haven't been going to choir rehearsals lately. Just can't keep my head straight for the hymns. And my garden... well, I've let parts of it just go to weed. Used to be I'd be out there every morning with my hoe. Bought that hoe at the old hardware store back before they built the bypass. You know, they put that bypass in to cut down on the logging trucks going through town, but all it did was run the diner out of business. Best cherry pie you ever had at that diner. The crust was real flaky, made with real lard. You can't find folks who bake with lard anymore, they all use that vegetable shortening stuff. Makes it taste like cardboard if you ask me. I tried to tell Mary that when she made a pie for Thanksgiving last year, but she got all huffy and told me to bake my own pie. Now, I don't know the first thing about baking. I can fry an egg, maybe make some toast, but that's about the extent of my cooking. I used to roast hot dogs on a stick when I was a boy, though...

What was the question again? Oh, right, how it affects my days. Yeah, it's just hard. Even the domino games down at the center... I guess with my mind jumping all over the place and talking about the messages and whatnot, I made things real uncomfortable for the other men. I don't even join 'em like I used to. Just easier to stay out of it.
Do you find it hard to have a conversation without jumping from one topic to another?

Well, like I was just telling you a minute ago, yes sir, it sure is. My mind just runs from the choir, over to baseball, then to the porch repairs, and back to my old friend again. It all goes so fast I just can't hold onto a single thought long enough to explain it right to anybody. I try to talk to folks, but the thoughts just won't sit still. 

Speaking of my friend, Jimmy... he had a porch that needed fixing too. The wood rot got into the bottom steps. We used to sit out there on this old wooden glider he had. Squeaked like a stepped-on mouse every time you rocked it. We tried greasing it with some of that 3-in-One oil. You know the kind, comes in that little tin can with the red spout? My daddy kept a can of that on his workbench for his pocket watch. He had this beautiful gold pocket watch, heavy thing, got it from his uncle who worked on the railroad. The trains used to come right through the center of town back then, blowing the whistle so loud it'd rattle the windows. I always wanted to ride the train out west to see the ocean... 

Wait, what were we... oh. Talking to people. Yeah, I can't keep the conversation straight because my head's just moving too quick.
Do you think the voices you hear, like your old friend calling your name, are coming from inside your head or from outside?

Well, that's the thing of it. Some afternoons, when the house is just... quiet, you know? I hear him clear as day. He'll call my name right from the porch, or maybe I'll hear him humming one of those old choir songs. It sounds like he's standing right there, right outside. 

We used to sit on that porch for hours. We'd watch the cars go by, back when there weren't so many on the road. Folks drove slower then. You had those big heavy cars, the kind with the metal dashboards. My brother had a Ford Fairlane, two-tone, blue and white. Kept it polished so bright you could see your reflection in the hubcaps. He used to take us down to the lake on Sundays. We'd fish for bluegill with just a cane pole and a worm. You dig the worms up yourself right out of the garden after a good rain. The soil was so rich back then. You don't see dirt like that anymore, it's all clay and rocks now. I tried growing tomatoes last year, but the blossom end rot got 'em. You gotta put crushed eggshells in the dirt for the calcium, my mother always said. She saved every eggshell in a little coffee can by the sink... 

What was I saying? Oh, the voices. Yeah, it's outside. It sounds like he's right there on the porch, calling for me.
Do you think it's possible that your mind is creating these messages as a way to cope with stress or anxiety?

Well, see, that's what Mary keeps telling me. She says I'm just getting worked up over nothing, that it's just talk. But it ain't just my mind making things up, Doctor. I know what I hear. The men down at the domino table, they slip these little messages into their talk, meant just for me. And sometimes the announcer on the radio does it too. They're warning me, telling me to be careful. 

Mary listens to that same radio station every morning. Wakes up at five-thirty sharp, turns on the farm report while she makes the coffee. We've had that same percolator since nineteen and seventy-two. Bought it at Sears and Roebuck. You remember when the Sears catalog used to come in the mail? Thick as a phone book, it was. You could buy anything out of that book. My uncle even bought a whole house out of a catalog once. Came in pieces on a train, and they put it together right there on the lot. A kit house, they called it. Had a big wrap-around porch. We'd sit on that porch and eat watermelon in the summer. You had to spit the seeds into the yard, though, or my aunt would pitch a fit. She kept her floors so clean you could eat off 'em. Used that Murphy's Oil Soap. Smelled like pine trees and lemons...

But no, to answer your question, it's not stress. The messages are real. They're trying to warn me, clear as day.

patient.answer:
Well, sometimes it feels like... like my mind is just running a mile a minute. It goes from thinking about the church choir on Sunday, to that baseball game I watched, then over to the repairs on the porch, and then to my friend down the street... all just bouncing around so fast.
